title: Aging‐Induced Ductile‐Brittle‐Ductile Transition in High‐Entropy Alloys and its Implications

recollection.starting_material: High-entropy alloy (likely a complex multi-principal element alloy, perhaps CoCrFeMnNi or a derivative)
recollection.intervention: Thermal aging treatments at various temperatures and durations to investigate microstructural evolution
recollection.structure: Probable precipitation of ordered intermetallic phases or short-range ordering domains within the fcc matrix, with accompanying changes in dislocation structures and grain-boundary segregation
recollection.mechanism: Aging first causes solid-solution hardening to give ductility, then precipitation/ordering leads to embrittlement, and at longer times coarsening or phase reversion restores some ductility—hence a ductile → brittle → ductile transition attributed to competition between strengthening precipitates, grain-boundary embrittlement, and recovery/recrystallization processes
recollection.results: Likely reports a peak in hardness and a drop in fracture toughness after intermediate aging (e.g., hardness increase ~20-30%, fracture toughness decrease by ~50%), followed by partial recovery of toughness at over-aging while strength remains moderately high. Specific numbers not recalled.

score.note: The recollection correctly identifies thermal aging and generically associates intermediate aging with ordering/precipitation-induced embrittlement followed by ductility recovery. However, it misses the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 FCC+B2 system, the specific 600°C and 750°C treatments, enhanced L12 ordering and jagged B2/FCC boundaries, and the APBE/cross-slip/plastic-instability mechanism. The proposed hardness and toughness percentages are unsupported and do not match reported quantitative details.
